title: ZPC cloud assets: asset types, categories and asset details

assets-vs-categories.statement: Asset types are cloud-service-provider-defined services, while asset categories are ZPC-specific aggregations of similar asset types across all providers (VMs and EC2 instances belong to the Compute category); each category includes multiple asset types.

quotes: Asset Types are services defined by the cloud service provider (CSP). For example, EC2 instances in Amazon Web Services (AWS) or virtual machines (VMs) in Microsoft Azure.
Asset Categories are ZPC-specific aggregations for similar asset types across all CSPs. For example, the VMs and EC2 instances belong to the Compute Asset category.
Each asset category includes multiple asset types.

asset-inventory-clouds.statement: The Cloud Asset Types and Asset Categories page says ZPC provides an inventory of asset types on Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud Platform and Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM).

quotes: ZPC provides an inventory of asset types on Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM).

public-exposure-asset-types.statement: Public exposure protection is supported for a listed subset of asset types per provider, including AWS EC2::SecurityGroup and ApiGatewayV2::APIs and Azure PublicIPAddresses.

quotes: ZPC supports the following CSP-defined asset types for public exposure protection:
EC2::SecurityGroup
ApiGatewayV2::APIs
PublicIPAddresses

databricks-not-listed.statement: Resources managed by Databricks are not listed in ZPC assets.

quotes: Resources managed by Databricks are not listed in ZPC assets.

azure-id-lowercase.statement: Azure asset IDs are displayed in lowercase regardless of the case in which they were created.

quotes: Azure Asset IDs are displayed in lowercase, regardless of the case in which they are originally created.

asset-list-fields.statement: ZPC shows per asset the first-discovery time (Discovered On), Publicly Exposed and Trusted IP flags and vulnerability count, and for Kubernetes assets the Cluster and Namespace where applicable.

quotes: Discovered On: The date and time when the asset was first discovered by ZPC.
Cluster: The Kubernetes cluster to which this asset belongs (if applicable).
Namespace: The namespace to which this asset belongs (if applicable).
Publicly Exposed: Whether the asset is publicly exposed or not.
Trusted IP: Whether the asset is associated with a trusted IP list or not.
Vulnerabilities: The number of vulnerabilities present on the asset.

asset-export-excel.statement: Cloud asset details can be exported as an Excel file.

quotes: Export the cloud asset details as an Excel file and download the report.

asset-timeline-retention.statement: The asset Timeline tab shows data for up to 6 months, and for AWS also the account ID and request parameters during resource state creation or update.

quotes: On the Timeline tab, you can do the following:
View the data for up to 6 months.
For AWS, you can also view the account ID and request parameters during resource state creation or update.

asset-alert-status-values.statement: On the asset Alerts tab the alert status is Open, Closed, Resolved or Ignored, and Alert Age is measured in days from the last time the status was set to Open; the Compliance Policies tab shows policy status Passed or Failed.

quotes: On the Alerts tab, you can do the following:
On the Compliance Policies tab, you can do the following:
Status: The status (Open, Closed, Resolved, or Ignored) of the alert.
Alert Age: The age of the alert (in days) from the last time the Alert Status was set to Open.
Status: The status of the security policy (Passed, Failed).

asset-trusted-ip-link.statement: When an asset is publicly exposed and associated with a trusted IP list, the publicly exposed attribute links to that list on the Trusted IP Management page.

quotes: When an asset is publicly exposed and associated with a trusted IP list, a link is provided against the publicly exposed attribute to navigate to the associated trusted IP list on the Trusted IP Management page.

asset-vuln-tab.statement: The asset Vulnerabilities tab covers assets within containers, lists packages with the highest CVE count and severity first, and exports the vulnerability data to a CSV file.

quotes: On the Vulnerabilities tab, you can do the following:
You can view the total number of vulnerabilities that ZPC detects in assets within containers
Packages with the highest count of CVEs and highest level of severity are listed first in the table.
Export the vulnerability data to a CSV file and download the report.

package-cve-fields.statement: Package vulnerability details show severity (Low, Medium, High or Critical), age of CVE and fix version, and all packages are displayed by default when the data is first viewed.

quotes: Severity: The severity level (Low, Medium, High, or Critical) of the vulnerability.
Age of CVE: The number of days the vulnerability was present in the source code when reported.
Fix Version: The package version that contains the vulnerability fix.
By default, all the packages are displayed when you first view the data.

asset-type-lists.title: Which asset types map to which asset categories
asset-type-lists.detail: The asset-type lists for AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes are long and were not claimed entry by entry; the AWS list repeats LoadBalancer, and names differ in spelling between the supported list and the public-exposure list (RouteTable and RouteTables, NetworkAcl, Sites and Websites). Categories such as Analyzer, Compute and Security are listed but only Compute has a stated member (VMs and EC2 instances).

service-status.title: Whether the ZPC features these pages describe are still available
service-status.detail: portfolio.cloud-protection records ZPC end of life as planned for March 15, 2026 (portfolio.cloud-protection:zpc-eos-eol). None of the captured asset pages says whether it describes a service still available, so none of the asset facts here is claimed as current.
